A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FD2 study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-distillation experiments, cross-architecture evaluations, ablations, visual analyses, and computational-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds ConvNeXt-Tiny evaluations, TESLA comparisons, attention-similarity measurements, and a class-supervision ablation.

M1.justification: The CAL teacher, prototype updates, fine-grained and similarity constraints, soft-label generation, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The newly ablated class-supervision loss Lcls already appears in v1's Equation 11.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same classification/distillation tasks on CUB-200-2011, FGVC-Aircraft, Stanford Cars, ImageNette, and ImageWoof. ConvNeXt-Tiny changes the student configuration, not dataset or task coverage. ImageNet-1K appears only as future work.

E2.justification: Supplementary Table 1 adds TESLA, printed as TELSA in the table, and removes the standalone SRe2L++ column from that comparison. SRe2L++ remains evaluated in the main text. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds ConvNeXt-Tiny student evaluation at IPC=3, a with/without-LS comparison using mean pairwise cosine similarity at NS=4, and an IPC=3 Lcls ablation. Existing benchmark resolutions, IPC budgets, and evaluation epochs remain unchanged; newly explicit teacher choices do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Figure 5 replaces the group-size heatmap sweep with a controlled with/without-LS diversity analysis. Supplementary Table 5 adds an Lcls ablation, and cross-architecture analysis adds ConvNeXt-Tiny. The lambda sensitivity study is relocated from appendix Table 4 to main Table 8, with unchanged results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new mean pairwise cosine similarity is a descriptive diversity metric, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged. New results include ConvNeXt-Tiny accuracies of 28.9/30.4 for SRe2L++ without/with FD2 and 29.1/35.1 for FADRM+ without/with FD2, nine TESLA accuracies, MPCS values of 0.77/0.63 without/with LS, and Lcls ablation accuracies of 60.0/57.2 with/without supervision. Table 3 incorrectly labels 29.1 to 35.1 as a 0.2-point increase.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and supplementary theoretical analysis are unchanged, including both propositions, both corollaries, their assumptions, and their proofs. Citation renumbering and relocation do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that FD2 augments decoupled distillation through CAL-derived supervision and two complementary constraints, improving fine-grained recognition and most evaluated settings. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions or their claimed scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies LS as improving diversity despite limited accuracy gains and interprets the new Lcls ablation as showing the importance of class-semantic supervision. The existing group-size saturation explanation remains. Future work now specifically names ViT-based models and ImageNet-1K.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised code release with a repository link and availability statement. Section 4.4 newly specifies ResNet18 as the SRe2L++ cross-architecture teacher, and Section 4.5 explains that NS=4 groups can run across multiple processes/GPUs. These are documentation additions, not demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning EVLF, parameter-pruning distillation, ConvNeXt, and vision-language category prototypes, while removing the earlier Improve cross-architecture generalization citation. The related-work organization and substantive positioning of FD2 remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify evaluation descriptions, move the lambda discussion into the main text, rename the appendix as supplementary material, revise author/affiliation information, and add acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redesigned, Table 3 gains a student row, supplementary Table 1 changes comparator columns, and a new supplementary ablation table appears. The lambda table moves into the main text and other ablation tables are rearranged. The remaining principal figures and appendix sample grids are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer teacher/student protocols, explicit code-access information, and the controlled attention-diversity comparison modestly improve transparency and empirical support. Added comparisons extend the evidence without changing the central findings. These benefits are tempered by the erroneous ConvNeXt gain annotation and the unexplained 60.0% supervised ablation control, which is not reconciled with the 64.9% IPC=3 result elsewhere. The net improvement is limited.
